svg.title: Japan at a glance
svg.desc: An editorial infographic about Japan: a stylized map with Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka and Nagoya; an overview; nominal GDP from 2015 to 2024 in current US dollars; population composition by nationality; and six places to visit.
svg.text: An island nation in East Asia
Geography, economy, people and places, on one page.
Main islands and the four largest cities

g.text: Japan is an archipelago of more than 14,000 islands
stretching about 3,000 km along the Pacific “Ring
of Fire”. Four main islands, Honshu, Hokkaido,
Kyushu and Shikoku, hold most of its 124 million
people, while forested mountains cover about three-
quarters of the land. Life crowds onto coastal plains,
where Greater Tokyo is the world’s largest metro area.

svg.text: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary government.

g.text: Few countries blend tradition and modernity as seamlessly. Japan has the world’s oldest continuous hereditary monarchy,
yet it gave the world the bullet train, karaoke and anime. Seasonal rituals, from cherry-blossom viewing in spring to
crimson maples in autumn, still shape the national calendar, and its famously punctual railways count delays in seconds.
An ageing, shrinking population is the defining challenge of the decades ahead.
Japan remains one of the world’s largest economies,
powered by cars, electronics, machinery and a deep
services sector. Measured in US dollars, output
peaked in 2019, then slid as the yen weakened
sharply from 2022, even while GDP in yen kept
rising. Exchange rates, not a slump, explain the dip.

svg.text: Dollar GDP fell about a fifth from its 2019 peak as the yen depreciated.
Population by nationality or ethnic group, %
Six classic stops for a first visit

g.text: Sources: GDP from World Bank World Development Indicators and IMF World Economic Outlook (nominal, current US$). Population composition: CIA World Factbook estimates.
City populations: municipal estimates, 2024 (Tokyo = Tokyo Metropolis). Figures rounded. Map is schematic; city positions are approximate.
